metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic, specifically isolating trials where TTB and Tallying make strictly opposing predictions (e.g., one option wins on the single most valid feature, while the other wins on a greater number of less valid features). For a simulated TTB agent, this proportion will be close to 1.0 (subject to epsilon noise). For a simulated Tallying agent, this proportion will be close to 0.0, as it reliably chooses the opposite option. This creates an enormous mean gap with very low between-subject variance.

By design, all trials in this experiment pit the Tallying heuristic directly against the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. Tallying always favors the option with the greater total number of positive features, while TTB always favors the opposite option (which wins on the single most valid discriminating cue). This metric simply computes the proportion of a subject's choices that align with the Tallying prediction. Under the Tallying theory, this proportion will be close to 1. Under the TTB theory, it will be close to 0. The gap is maximized, and within-theory variance is minimized.
